chapter: Publishing, Jelly Roll in Los Angeles and band lore
title: Hegamin, Murray and the Johnson family
summary: The imported pianist was Lucille Hegamin's husband, Murray owned the Cadillac, and Bill and Dink Johnson were brothers of Anita.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: It's 1917. Right. And then he said that they brought in...ah, a piano player from back East--Hageman.

And they brought him in as a pianist, and, uh, that was when Jelly Roll left and went to, he says, George Brown's place and took all the movie star trade... "By that time the Cadillac was sure I was the man so I took over half the business, went back in there..."

Murray owned the Cadillac. He played at the Cadillac, and that is the time I was running the Dreamland...no, I don't remember now, I think so. And see, I run the...opened up the music store and one...uh, in '20. Christmas, 1919. And about February or March, we opened the Dreamland, the nightclub. Just a few months--two, three months afterward.

I see. Oh. Yeah, yeah, he makes a distinction between the 1917 and the 1922. I'm sorry. I was running it together here, trying to read fast. He said he'd "often seen my brother-in-law, Bill Johnson"--is that Dink Johnson?
No, Bill Johnson was a...Dink Johnson's brother.
I see. There were two brothers.
Yeah. He said brother-in-law, didn't he? See, then he was...uh, that girl was Dink's and Bill's sister.
